paragraphs: Sterling Infrastructure, Inc. ("Sterling" or "the Company") operates through a variety of subsidiaries within three segments specializing in E-Infrastructure, Transportation and Building Solutions in the United States, primarily across the Southern, Northeastern, Mid-Atlantic and Rocky Mountain regions and the Pacific Islands. E-Infrastructure Solutions provides advanced, large-scale site development services and mission-critical electrical services for data centers, semiconductor fabrication, manufacturing, distribution centers, warehousing, power generation and more. Transportation Solutions includes infrastructure and rehabilitation projects for highways, roads, bridges, airports, ports, rail and storm drainage systems. Building Solutions includes residential and commercial concrete foundations for single-family and multi-family homes, parking structures, elevated slabs, other concrete work, plumbing services, and surveys for new single-family residential builds. From strategy to operations, we are committed to sustainability by operating responsibly to safeguard and improve society's quality of life. Caring for our people and our communities, our customers and our investors – that is The Sterling Way.

In this report, unless the context otherwise indicates, "Sterling," "the Company," "we," "our" or "us" means Sterling and its consolidated subsidiaries. In addition, references to "Note" or "Notes" refer to the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, included in Item 8 of Part II of this annual report on Form 10-K, unless indicated otherwise.
Since 2016, our strategic vision has been based on the following elements and objectives:
Solidifying the base Risk Reduction Growing high margin products and services Bottom-Line Growth
Expansion into adjacent markets Exceed Peer Performance Build a Platform for Future Accretive Growth

Solidifying the base—The first element of the transformation of the Company that began in 2016 was a deep evaluation of the risks and opportunities associated with our project portfolio. We continue to work to move the business toward the opportunities that provide the most favorable risk/reward dynamics.

Prior to 2015, the company's historic base of business was low-bid heavy highway projects within the Transportation Solutions segment; gross margins on these projects during this time were approximately 4%. In 2016, we implemented a strategy to solidify the business by improving risk assessment and bid discipline to significantly reduce the probability of project losses. This strategy has been successful, more than doubling the gross margins of heavy highway projects. In early 2025, we announced the strategic downsizing of our Texas heavy highway business, which is expected to be complete in 2026. This is anticipated to drive further improvement in heavy highway margins.

In recent years, our efforts to solidify the base business have been focused on driving productivity across each of our businesses, developing talent and trades people to support the growth of the company and our industries, and expanding our use of technology across the company to enhance our operations and support growth. Further, we are focused on continual safety enhancements across the organization.

Growing high margin products and services—Across our organization, we are focused on pursuing the most attractive project opportunities from a margin and return perspective. This was a key element of the transformation of the company from 2015 through 2019 and remains a key pillar of our strategy today. The focus in this strategic area is to drive consistent, strong bottom-line growth.

In 2016, we implemented a strategy to shift our Transportation Solutions project mix from low-bid heavy highway projects to alternative delivery heavy highway projects and other higher margin work including airports, commercial, piling and shoring and rail. In 2016, our low-bid heavy highway revenue was approximately 79% of our total revenue, but we have progressively lowered this to 9% as of December 31, 2025.

In E-Infrastructure Solutions, we have built a reputation for strong execution across large, multifaceted, time-sensitive projects for mission-critical customers. In our site development business, our ability to consistently provide on-time delivery and schedule assurance to our customers through successful project management and execution has become a key source of competitive differentiation, and a factor in our margin profile. In the electrical and mechanical business, we have a strong track record of delivering high-performance electrical solutions for the most demanding mission-critical clients. Our focus on large, time-sensitive mission-critical projects where our superior capabilities are valued by our customers has been a driver of segment margin expansion over time and remains our focus moving forward.

Expansion into adjacent markets—In 2016, we implemented a strategy to pursue growth through the acquisition of companies and assets that will enable us to expand into adjacent markets and broaden the types of projects we execute. We operate a decentralized, adaptive business model, which provides us with flexibility to pursue acquisitions and other strategic transactions. Our acquisition strategy focuses on businesses that can enhance our suite of products and services, expand our geographic footprint or customer relationships, or provide diversification of cash flows. Since 2016, we have completed eleven acquisitions and regularly assess other strategic opportunities. Further, we remain focused on opportunities to expand organically into new markets.

RHB Deconsolidation—Since 2012, the Company has held a 50% ownership interest in Road and Highway Builders, LLC ("RHB"), with Rich Buenting holding the remaining 50% ownership interest. Historically, the Company fully consolidated the entity as a result of its exercise of control of the entity. On December 31, 2024, the parties executed an amendment to the RHB operating agreement to ensure the continuation of this mutually beneficial relationship while addressing the evolving needs and interest of both parties.

Under GAAP, this contractual change required Sterling to no longer consolidate RHB's results with its own and to use equity method accounting with respect to Sterling's interest in the entity. Beginning January 1, 2025, the Company reports its portion of RHB's income as a single line item ("Other operating income (expense), net") in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and reports its interest in RHB at December 31, 2024 and thereafter, as a single line item ("Investment in unconsolidated subsidiary") in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. RHB's revenue is no longer included in Sterling's consolidated revenue in 2025 and Sterling's consolidated backlog figures as of December 31, 2024 and thereafter, do not include RHB's backlog.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Demand for our services may decrease during economic recessions or volatile economic cycles, and a reduction in demand in end markets may adversely affect our business.
Our dependence on suppliers of materials and subcontractors could increase our costs and impair our ability to complete contracts on a timely basis or at all.
We may incur higher costs to lease, acquire and maintain equipment necessary for our operations, and the market value of our owned equipment may decline.
We may not accurately assess and/or estimate the quality, quantity, availability and cost of aggregates we need to complete a project, particularly for projects in rural areas.
Timing of the award and performance of new contracts may fluctuate.
Adverse weather conditions may cause delays, which could slow completion of our construction activity.
We rely on information technology systems to conduct our business, which are subject to disruption, failure or security breaches.
Major public health crises could disrupt our operations and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Risks Related to Our Segments

Our E-Infrastructure Solutions business, as well as the industries of many of our customers upon whom we are dependent, are susceptible to economic downturns, including periods of slower than anticipated economic growth.
Our Transportation Solutions business relies on highly competitive and highly regulated state or local government contracts.
The design-build project delivery method subjects our Transportation Solutions business to the risk of design errors and omissions.
An inability to obtain bonding could limit the aggregate dollar amount of contracts that we are able to pursue for our Transportation Solutions business.
Our Transportation Solutions business is susceptible to economic downturns and reductions in state or local government funding of infrastructure projects.
A prolonged government shutdown may adversely affect our Transportation Solutions business.
Risks Related to Our Construction Joint Venture Partners and Customers
Our participation in construction joint ventures exposes us to liability and/or harm to our reputation for failures of our partners.
We may not be able to recover on claims or change orders against clients for payment or on claims against subcontractors for performance.
We are dependent on a limited number of significant customers.
The early termination of contracts and uncertainty of new project awards could adversely affect our business.
Risks Related to Our Workforce
Our business depends on our ability to attract and retain talented employees.
We may be subject to unionization, work stoppages, slowdowns or increased labor costs.
If we are unable to comply with applicable immigration laws, our ability to successfully complete contracts may be negatively impacted.
We contribute to multiemployer plans that could result in liabilities to us if those plans are terminated or if we withdraw from those plans.
Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters
We are, and may continue to be, involved in routine litigation and government inquiries in the ordinary course of business.

Recent and potential changes in U.S. trade policies and retaliatory responses from other countries may significantly increase the costs or limit supplies of materials and products used in our projects.
Tax matters, including changes in corporate tax laws and disagreements with taxing authorities, could impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Our business is subject to complex and evolving laws and regulations regarding data privacy and cybersecurity.
We use artificial intelligence ("AI") technologies in our business, and the deployment, use, and maintenance of these technologies involve significant technological and legal risks.
Risks Related to Strategy and Acquisitions
Our strategy, which includes expanding into adjacent markets, may not be successful.
Risks Related to Our Financial Results, Financing and Liquidity

Our use of over time revenue recognition (formerly known as percentage-of-completion method) accounting related to our projects could result in a reduction or elimination of previously reported revenue and profits.
We may not be able to fully realize the revenue value reported in our Backlog.
Our Credit Agreement contains various covenants and other provisions that impose restrictions on our ability to operate and manage our business.
paragraphs: The following discussion of risk factors contains forward-looking statements. These risk factors may be important to understanding other statements in this annual report on Form 10-K. The following information should be read in conjunction with Part II, Item 7 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes in Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this annual report on Form 10-K.

Our business, financial condition and operating results can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including but not limited to those described below; any one or more of which could, directly or indirectly, cause our actual financial condition and operating results to vary materially from our past, or from our anticipated future, financial condition and operating results. Any of these factors, including additional factors that apply to all companies generally which are not specifically mentioned below, in whole or in part, could materially and adversely affect our business, prospects, financial condition, results of operations, stock price and cash flows.

Because of the following factors, as well as other factors affecting our financial condition and operating results, our past financial performance should not be considered to be a reliable indicator of our future performance, and investors should not use historical trends to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

Across our three operating segments, revenue and profit are generated from infrastructure projects and services, but we do not directly control the process by which such infrastructure projects and services are awarded. The construction industry historically has experienced cyclical fluctuations in financial results due to economic recessions, downturns in business cycles of our customers, supply chain disruptions and the price or availability of building materials, inflationary pressures, interest rate fluctuations, international trade issues, including tariffs and counter tariffs, and other economic factors beyond our control. Many factors, including the financial condition of the infrastructure industry, could adversely affect our customers and their willingness to fund capital expenditures in the future. Additionally, consolidation, competition or capital constraints in the industries we serve may result in reduced spending by our customers.

Economic, regulatory and market conditions affecting our specific end markets may adversely impact the demand for our services, resulting in the delay, reduction or cancellation of certain projects and these conditions may continue to adversely affect us in the future.

The price and availability of the materials required to execute our projects are subject to volatility and disruptions caused by global economic factors that are beyond our control, including, but not limited to, labor shortages, wage pressures, rising inflation and potential economic slowdown or recession, as well as fuel and energy costs, the impact of natural disasters, geopolitical conflicts (such as the conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East), and other matters that have impacted or could impact the global economy. If shortages and cost increases in materials and tightness in the labor market persist for a prolonged period of time, and we are unable to offset such cost increases, our profit margins could be adversely impacted.

paragraphs: The following "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" is provided to assist readers in understanding our financial performance during the periods presented and significant trends that may impact our future performance. This discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and the related notes thereto.

General—Sterling operates through a variety of subsidiaries within three segments specializing in E-Infrastructure, Transportation and Building Solutions in the United States, primarily across the Southern, Northeastern, Mid-Atlantic and Rocky Mountain regions and the Pacific Islands. E-Infrastructure Solutions provides advanced, large-scale site development services and mission-critical electrical services for data centers, semiconductor fabrication, manufacturing, distribution centers, warehousing, power generation and more. Transportation Solutions includes infrastructure and rehabilitation projects for highways, roads, bridges, airports, ports, rail and storm drainage systems. Building Solutions includes residential and commercial concrete foundations for single-family and multi-family homes, parking structures, elevated slabs, other concrete work, plumbing services, and surveys for new single-family residential builds. From strategy to operations, we are committed to sustainability by operating responsibly to safeguard and improve society's quality of life. Caring for our people and our communities, our customers and our investors – that is The Sterling Way.

RHB Deconsolidation—Since 2012, the Company has held a 50% ownership interest in Road and Highway Builders, LLC ("RHB"), with Rich Buenting holding the remaining 50% ownership interest. Historically, the Company fully consolidated the entity as a result of its exercise of control of the entity. On December 31, 2024, the parties executed an amendment to the RHB operating agreement to ensure the continuation of this mutually beneficial relationship while addressing the evolving needs and interest of both parties. This amendment modified the way RHB would be dispositioned in the event of the death or disability of Mr. Buenting and provides that in such event, Sterling and Mr. Buenting's estate must agree on one of four alternatives: (1) continuation of the existing ownership structure, (2) acquisition of Sterling's 50% interest by Mr. Buenting's estate at fair market value, (3) acquisition of Mr. Buenting's 50% interest by Sterling at fair market value or (4) the joint sale of RHB to a third party at fair market value.

Under GAAP, this contractual change required Sterling to no longer consolidate RHB's results with its own and to use equity method accounting with respect to Sterling's interest in the entity. Beginning January 1, 2025, the Company reports its portion of RHB's income as a single line item ("Other operating income (expense), net") in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and reports its interest in RHB at December 31, 2024, and thereafter, as a single line item ("Investment in unconsolidated subsidiary") in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. RHB's revenue is no longer included in Sterling's consolidated revenue in 2025 and Sterling's consolidated backlog figures as of December 31, 2024, and thereafter, do not include RHB's backlog.

Drake Acquisition—During the first quarter of 2025, Sterling acquired Drake Concrete, LLC ("Drake") (the "Drake Acquisition"). Drake provides concrete slabs for residential home builders in the Dallas-Fort Worth market. The acquisition strengthens Sterling's geographic footprint within the DFW metroplex and expands and deepens the customer base, given limited customer overlap with Tealstone. The purchase price was $25 million in cash plus a four year earn-out opportunity. The results of Drake are included in our Building Solutions segment.

CEC Acquisition—On September 1, 2025, the Company acquired substantially all of the assets of Irving, Texas-based CEC Facilities Group, LLC ("CEC") a leading specialty electrical and mechanical contractor. The purchase price was $562 million, consisting primarily of $443 million in cash and $79 million in common stock. Additionally, CEC has an earn-out opportunity of up to an aggregate of $80 million, contingent upon achieving certain operating income targets. CEC is included in the Company's E-Infrastructure Solutions segment.

We see favorable opportunities for long-term growth across each of our business segments. We remain focused on our strategic objectives, as described in Item 1 "Business — Business Strategy." These objectives include: 1) growth in our E-Infrastructure Solutions segment, with particular focus on large, high-value projects; 2) risk reduction through a continued shift in our Transportation Solutions business away from low-bid heavy highway work, and toward alternative delivery and design-build projects; 3) continuing to grow market share and geographic presence in Building Solutions; and 4) improving our margins in each of our segments.

E-Infrastructure Solutions—Our E-Infrastructure Solutions business is driven by our customers' investments in the development of data centers, advanced manufacturing centers, e-commerce distribution centers and warehouses. We foresee significant growth opportunities tied to the implementation of multi-year capital deployment plans by data center customers, including hyperscalers, colocation providers and others. These investments are driven by the need to support the increasing use of cloud computing applications, increasing adoption and complexity of artificial intelligence applications and digital transformation across industries. Additionally, we continue to see significant opportunity related to the construction of manufacturing capacity in the U.S., including semiconductor fabrication. Following a decline that began in 2023, the e-commerce distribution sector began to strengthen in 2025 and we expect this momentum to continue in 2026.

Transportation Solutions—Our Transportation Solutions business is primarily driven by federal, state and municipal funding. Federal funds, on average, provide 50% of annual State Department of Transportation capital outlays for highway and bridge projects. We benefit from a number of federal, state and local infrastructure investment programs. At the Federal level, the Infrastructure Investments and Jobs Act ("IIJA"), which establishes funding for the fiscal 2022 through 2026 time period, drove significant increases in transportation funding relative to the previous five-year law. The IIJA includes approximately $643 billion in funding for transportation programs ($432 billion for highways, $109 billion for transportation and $102 billion for rail), of which $284 billion is an increase over historic investment levels that will fund new transportation infrastructure. The IIJA also includes $25 billion of funding for airport modernization. As a result of the IIJA, we saw an increase in bid activity and project awards which started in the third quarter of 2022 and continued through 2025. In 2026, we expect that the combination of strong state-level funding in our core geographies and elevated federal funding will allow the transportation market to remain strong relative to historical levels.

Building Solutions—Our Building Solutions segment is comprised of our residential and commercial businesses. The segment is driven by new home starts in Dallas-Fort Worth, the segment's largest market, and continued expansion in the Houston and Phoenix markets. Building Solutions' core customer base includes top national, regional and custom home builders in our areas. Beginning in the second half of 2024, demand from residential home builder customers began to decline, as prospective homebuyers struggled with affordability challenges. We anticipate that demand will remain muted in the near-term, but believe the dynamics in our markets, including population growth and structural housing shortages, support a return to growth over a multi-year time period.

Our remaining performance obligations on our projects, as defined in ASC 606, do not differ from what we refer to as "Backlog." Our Backlog represents the amount of revenues we expect to recognize in the future from our contract commitments on projects. The contracts in Backlog are typically completed in 6 to 36 months. Our unsigned awards ("Unsigned Awards") are excluded from Backlog until the contract is executed by our customer. We refer to the combination of our Backlog and Unsigned Awards as "Combined Backlog." Our book-to-burn ratio is determined by taking our additions to Backlog and dividing it by revenue for the applicable period. This metric allows management to monitor the Company's business development efforts to ensure we grow our Backlog and our business over time, and management believes that this measure is useful to investors for the same reason.

At December 31, 2025, our Backlog was $3.01 billion, as compared to $1.69 billion at December 31, 2024, with a book-to-burn ratio of 1.6X for the year ended December 31, 2025. Included in Backlog at December 31, 2025 is $488.9 million contributed from the electrical and mechanical business acquired late in the third quarter 2025. The Company's margin in Backlog has increased to 17.8% at December 31, 2025 from 16.7% at December 31, 2024, driven by a greater mix of E-Infrastructure Solutions backlog and an improved backlog margin mix within Transportation Solutions.

Unsigned Awards were $300.7 million at December 31, 2025 and $137.9 million at December 31, 2024. Included in Unsigned Awards at December 31, 2025 is $226.4 million contributed from the electrical and mechanical business acquired late in the third quarter 2025. Combined Backlog totaled $3.31 billion and $1.83 billion at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, with a book-to-burn ratio of 1.7X for the year ended December 31, 2025.

paragraphs: Sterling Infrastructure, Inc. ("Sterling" or "the Company") 透過多種子公司，於美國三個應報告分部運作，專門從事 E-Infrastructure、Transportation 和 Building Solutions，主要服務區域為南方、東北方、中大西洋及洛磯山脈地區，以及太平洋羣島。E-Infrastructure 解決方案提供先進、大規模的場地開發服務與關鍵任務電力服務，用於資料中心、半導體製造、製造、配送中心、倉儲、電力發電等。Transportation 解決方案包括高速公路、道路、橋樑、機場、港口、鐵路及暴雨排水系統的基礎建設與修復工程。Building 解決方案包括單戶與多戶住宅的住宅與商業混凝土基礎、停車場結構、高架樓板、其他混凝土工程、給排水服務，以及新興單戶住宅的測繪服務。從戰略到運作，我們致力於永續發展，透過負責任的運作來保障並提升社會的生活品質。關懷我們的員工與社區、客戶與投資者，這就是 The Sterling Way。
在本報告中，除非上下文另有說明，"Sterling"、"the Company"、"we"、"our" 或 "us" 均指 Sterling 及其合併子公司。此外，提及 "Note" 或 "Notes" 時，均指包含於本年度 10-K 表報表第二部分第 8 項的合併財務報表附註，除非另有說明。
自 2016 年起，我們的戰略願景基於以下要素與目標：
強化基礎 風險降低 高毛利率產品與服務 底線成長
擴張至鄰近市場 超越同業表現 建立未來可擴張成長的平台
強化基礎—自 2016 年開始的公司轉型第一個要素，是對我們專案組合所涉及的風險與機會進行深入評估。我們持續努力將業務轉向提供最優風險/報酬動態的機會。
在 2015 年之前，公司的歷史業務基礎為 Transportation 解決方案分部的低標高額公路專案；此時期這些專案的毛利率約為 4%。2016 年，我們實施了一項策略，透過改善風險評估與投標紀律，來大幅降低專案虧損的機率。此策略已成功，使高額公路專案的毛利率超過倍增。2025 年初，我們宣佈將縮減德克薩斯州的高額公路業務，預計於 2026 年完成。這預期將進一步提升高額公路專案的毛利率。
近年來，我們強化基礎業務的努力，著重於提升各業務的生產力、培養人才與技工以支持公司與產業的成長，並擴大公司在各部門的科技應用，以提升運作效率並支持成長。此外，我們也持續著重於組織內的持續安全改進。
發展高毛利率的產品與服務—在本公司內，我們致力於追求從毛利率與回報角度而言最具吸引力的專案機會。這是在2015年至2019年間公司轉型的關鍵要素，並仍然是我們當前策略的重要支柱。此戰略領域的重點在於推動持續且強勁的營運績效成長。
2016年，我們實施了一項策略，將交通解決方案專案組合從低標價的重載公路專案轉向替代性交付的重載公路專案及其他更高毛利率的工作，包括機場、商業、樁基與支撐結構以及鐵路。2016年，我們的低標價重載公路營業收入約佔總營業收入的79%，但我們已逐步降低至2025年12月31日的9%。

在E-基礎設施解決方案部門，我們已建立在執行大型、多面向、時間敏感專案方面的強大聲譽，以服務至關重要的客戶。在我們的場地開發業務中，我們能透過成功的專案管理與執行，持續提供準時交付與排程保障給客戶，這已成為我們競爭優勢的重要來源，並影響我們的毛利率表現。在電氣與機械業務中，我們有強大的紀錄，能為最嚴苛的至關重要的客戶提供高性能的電氣解決方案。我們專注於大型、時間敏感的至關重要的專案，這些專案中我們的優越能力受到客戶的重視，這已成為段落毛利率擴張的驅動力，並持續成為我們未來的重點。

擴展至鄰近市場—2016年，我們實施了一項策略，透過收購公司與資產來追求成長，這些公司與資產將使我們能擴展至鄰近市場並廣泛執行不同類型的專案。我們運作一個分散式、靈活的商業模式，這使我們能靈活追求收購及其他戰略交易。我們的收購策略聚焦於能提升我們產品與服務組合、擴展我們地理足跡或客戶關係，或提供現金流多樣化的業務。自2016年起，我們已完成十一項收購，並持續評估其他戰略機會。此外，我們仍專注於有機擴展至新市場的機會。
RHB 解構—自2012年起，本公司持有Road and Highway Builders, LLC（"RHB"）50%的股權，Rich Buenting持有剩餘50%的股權。歷來，本公司因行使對該公司的控制權而完全合併該公司。2024年12月31日，雙方簽訂了RHB營運協議的修正案，以確保這項互利關係的持續，同時回應雙方不斷變化的需要與利益。

根據GAAP，此契約變更要求Sterling不再合併RHB的營運結果，並對Sterling在該公司的權益使用權益法會計。自2025年1月1日起，本公司將其在RHB的收益部分作為單一項目（"其他營運收入（費用），淨額"）列示在合併營運損益表中，並將其在RHB的權益於2024年12月31日及之後作為單一項目（"未合併子公司投資"）列示在合併資產負債表中。RHB的營業收入不再包含在Sterling的合併營業收入中，且Sterling的合併待執行專案數目自2024年12月31日起不再包含RHB的待執行專案數目。

paragraphs: 以下為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，旨在協助讀者瞭解我們在所列期間的財務表現以及可能影響未來表現的重大趨勢。此討論應與我們的合併財務報表及相關附註同時閱讀。

總體—Sterling 透過三個分部內的多個子公司運作，專門從事 E-Infrastructure、運輸及建築解決方案，主要服務美國南部、東北部、中大西洋及洛基山地區以及太平洋羣島。E-Infrastructure 解決方案提供先進、大規模的場地開發服務及關鍵電力服務，用於資料中心、半導體製造、製造、分銷中心、倉儲、電力發電等。運輸解決方案包括高速公路、道路、橋樑、機場、港口、鐵路及暴雨排水系統的基礎建設與修復工程。建築解決方案包括單戶與多戶住宅的住宅與商業混凝土基礎、停車結構、高架樓板、其他混凝土工程、給排水服務及新興單戶住宅建設的測繪服務。從策略到營運，我們致力於永續發展，以負責任的方式運作，以保障並提升社會的生活品質。關懷我們的員工與社區、客戶與投資者，這就是 The Sterling Way。

RHB 解散—自 2012 年起，本公司持有 Road and Highway Builders, LLC（"RHB"）50% 的股權，Rich Buenting 持有剩餘的 50% 股權。歷來，本公司因行使控制權而將該實體完全合併。2024 年 12 月 31 日，雙方簽訂 RHB 管理協議的修正案，以確保此互利關係的持續，同時回應雙方不斷變化的需求與利益。此修正案修改了 RHB 在 Mr. Buenting 死亡或失能時的處置方式，並規定在此情況下，Sterling 與 Mr. Buenting 的遺產必須協議選擇四種替代方案之一：(1) 繼續現有股權結構，(2) Mr. Buenting 的遺產以公平市價購入 Sterling 的 50% 股權，(3) Sterling 以公平市價購入 Mr. Buenting 的 50% 股權，或 (4) 聯合將 RHB 賣給第三方，以公平市價進行。

根據 GAAP，此契約變更要求 Sterling 不再將 RHB 的結果與自身合併，並針對 Sterling 在該實體的權益使用權益法會計。自 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，本公司將其在 RHB 的收入作為單一項目（"其他營運收入（費用），淨額"）列示於合併營運表中，並將其在 RHB 的權益於 2024 年 12 月 31 日及之後，作為單一項目（"未合併子公司投資"）列示於合併資產負債表中。RHB 的收入不再包含於 Sterling 的合併收入中，且 Sterling 的合併待履行訂單數目於 2024 年 12 月 31 日及之後，亦不包含 RHB 的待履行訂單。

Drake 收購—於 2025 年第一季，Sterling 收購 Drake Concrete, LLC（"Drake"）（"Drake 收購"）。Drake 提供住宅房屋建造商在達拉斯-沃斯堡市場的混凝土樓板。此收購強化了 Sterling 在 DFW 地區的地理足跡，並擴大並深化客戶基礎，因與 Tealstone 的客戶重疊有限。收購價格為 2500 萬美元現金加上四年的 earn-out 機會。Drake 的營運結果已納入我們的建築解決方案分部。

CEC 收購—於 2025 年 9 月 1 日，本公司收購位於德克薩斯州伊溫格的 CEC Facilities Group, LLC（"CEC"），為一家領先的專業電氣與機械承包商。收購價格為 5.62 億美元，主要為 4.43 億美元現金及 7900 萬美元普通股。此外，CEC 還有最高達 8000 萬美元的 earn-out 機會，條件為達成特定營運收入目標。CEC 已納入本公司的 E-Infrastructure 解決方案分部。

我們看到各個業務分部均有長遠成長的優勢機會。我們持續專注於我們的戰略目標，如 Item 1 "業務 — 業務策略" 所述。這些目標包括：1) 在 E-Infrastructure 解決方案分部實現成長，特別是針對大型、高價值的項目；2) 透過持續將運輸解決方案業務從低標重載公路工程轉向替代性交付與設計建造項目，來降低風險；3) 繼續在建築解決方案分部擴大市場佔有率與地理足跡；以及 4) 改進各個分部的毛利率。

E-Infrastructure 解決方案—我們的 E-Infrastructure 解決方案業務由客戶在資料中心、先進製造中心、電商分銷中心與倉儲設施的發展投資所驅動。我們預見與資料中心客戶實施多年度資本部署計畫相關的重大成長機會，包括超規模資料中心、共用空間服務提供商及其他相關機構。這些投資由支持雲端計算應用的日益增加、人工智慧應用的採用與複雜度提升以及產業數位轉型的需要所驅動。此外，我們持續看到與美國製造能力建設相關的重大機會，包括半導體製造。自 2023 年開始的下降趨勢於 2025 年開始強化，我們預期此動能將在 2026 年持續。

Transportation Solutions—本公司 Transportation Solutions 商業主要由聯邦、州及市級資金驅動。聯邦資金，平均而言，提供每年州交通部資本支出的 50% 用於公路和橋樑項目。本公司受益於多項聯邦、州及地方基礎建設投資計畫。在聯邦層面，基礎建設投資與就業法案（"IIJA"），該法案為 2022 至 2026 財政年度設立資金，導致交通資金相較於前五年的法律顯著增加。IIJA 包含約 6430 億美元用於交通計畫的資金（4320 億美元用於公路，1090 億美元用於交通及 1020 億美元用於鐵路），其中 2840 億美元為歷史投資水平的增加，將用於新交通基礎建設。IIJA 還包含 250 億美元用於機場現代化。由於 IIJA，我們在 2022 年第三季開始並持續至 2025 年看到招標活動和項目授標增加。在 2026 年，我們預期強勁的州級資金在核心地理區域以及提高的聯邦資金將使交通市場相較於歷史水平保持強勁。

Building Solutions—Our Building Solutions segment is comprised of our residential and commercial businesses. The segment is driven by new home starts in Dallas-Fort Worth, the segment's largest market, and continued expansion in the Houston and Phoenix markets. Building Solutions' core customer base includes top national, regional and custom home builders in our areas. Beginning in the second half of 2024, demand from residential home builder customers began to decline, as prospective homebuyers struggled with affordability challenges. We anticipate that demand will remain muted in the near-term, but believe the dynamics in our markets, including population growth and structural housing shortages, support a return to growth over a multi-year time period.

Our remaining performance obligations on our projects, as defined in ASC 606, do not differ from what we refer to as "Backlog." Our Backlog represents the amount of revenues we expect to recognize in the future from our contract commitments on projects. The contracts in Backlog are typically completed in 6 to 36 months. Our unsigned awards ("Unsigned Awards") are excluded from Backlog until the contract is executed by our customer. We refer to the combination of our Backlog and Unsigned Awards as "Combined Backlog." Our book-to-burn ratio is determined by taking our additions to Backlog and dividing it by revenue for the applicable period. This metric allows management to monitor the Company's business development efforts to ensure we grow our Backlog and our business over time, and management believes that this measure is useful to investors for the same reason.

於2025年12月31日，本公司的待履行訂單為30.1億美元，較2024年12月31日的16.9億美元增加，全年待履行訂單與履行比率為1.6倍。於2025年12月31日的待履行訂單中，包含來自2025年第三季末取得之電機與機械業務的4.889億美元。本公司的待履行訂單毛利率於2025年12月31日提高至17.8%，較2024年12月31日的16.7%增加，主因為E-基礎建設解決方案的待履行訂單比例增加，以及交通解決方案的待履行訂單毛利率結構改善。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
在經濟衰退或波動經濟週期期間，對我們服務之需求可能下降，而終端市場需求之減少可能對我們業務造成不利影響。
我們對材料供應商及 subcontractors 之依賴可能增加我們成本，並影響我們按時或完全完成合約之能力。
我們可能因租用、購置及維護營運所需設備而產生更高成本，且我們自有設備之市場價值可能下降。
我們可能無法準確評估及/或預估完成專案所需之 aggregates 之品質、數量、可取得性及成本，特別是在鄉村地區之專案。
新合約之授與及執行時程可能有所波動。
惡劣天氣條件可能導致延誤，進而減緩我們之建設活動完成速度。
我們依賴資訊科技系統進行營運，這些系統可能受到中斷、故障或安全入侵之影響。
重大公共衛生危機可能幹擾我們的營運，並對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
與本公司應報告分部相關的風險
本公司 E-Infrastructure Solutions 事業，以及許多客戶所屬產業（本公司業務依賴這些客戶），均易受經濟衰退影響，包括經濟成長低於預期的時期。
本公司 Transportation Solutions 事業依賴高度競爭且受嚴格規範的州或地方政府契約。
設計建造（design-build）的項目交付方式，使本公司 Transportation Solutions 事業面臨設計錯誤或遺漏的風險。
無法取得擔保可能限制本公司 Transportation Solutions 事業所能追尋的契約總金額。
本公司 Transportation Solutions 事業易受經濟衰退及州或地方政府基礎建設項目經費減少的影響。
政府長時間停擺可能對本公司 Transportation Solutions 事業造成不利影響。
與本公司建設合資企業夥伴及客戶相關之風險
本公司參與建設合資企業可能使本公司面臨因夥伴失敗而產生之責任或聲譽損害。
本公司可能無法就對客戶之索賠或變更指令取得付款，或就對分包商之索賠取得履行。
本公司依賴少數重要客戶。
合約提前終止及新項目獲獎之不確定性可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
與本公司員工相關之風險
本公司業務取決於本公司吸引及留住優秀員工之能力。
本公司可能面臨工會化、停工、減產或勞動成本增加之風險。
若我們無法遵守適用的移民法規，將可能影響我們成功完成契約的能力。
我們參與多僱主計畫，若這些計畫終止或我們退出這些計畫，可能會導致我們產生負債。
與法律及法規相關的風險
我們可能持續涉及常規業務運作中的訴訟及政府調查。
美國近期及潛在的貿易政策變動及他國的報復性回應，可能顯著提高我們專案中所使用材料及產品的成本或限制供應。
稅務事項，包括企業稅法的變動及與稅務機關的爭議，可能影響我們的營運成果及財務狀況。
我們的業務受涉及資料隱私及網路安全的複雜且不斷演進的法律及法規所規範。
我們在業務中使用人工智慧（"AI"）技術，這些技術的部署、使用及維護涉及重大技術及法律風險。
與策略及併購相關之風險
本公司之策略，包含擴展至相鄰市場，可能無法成功。
與本公司財務結果、融資及流動性相關之風險
本公司於項目相關之收入認列（ formerly known as percentage-of-completion method）使用逾時收入認列會導致先前報導之收入及利潤減少或消除。
本公司可能無法完全實現背負之收入價值。
本公司信用協議包含多項契約條款及其他規定，限制本公司經營及管理業務之能力。
paragraphs: 以下有關風險因素的討論包含前瞻性陳述。這些風險因素可能對理解本年度報表（Form 10-K）中其他陳述具有重要性。以下資訊應與本年度報表（Form 10-K）第二部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」以及第二部分，第8項「財務報表與補充資料」中的合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。
我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果可能受多種因素影響，無論是否為目前已知或未知，包括但不限於以下所列因素；任何一個或數個因素，可能直接或間接導致我們的實際財務狀況與營運成果與我們過去或預期未來的財務狀況與營運成果產生重大差異。任何這些因素，包括適用於所有公司的一般因素，且未在以下明確提及，整體或部分，都可能對我們的業務、前景、財務狀況、營運成果、股票價格與現金流產生重大且不利的影響。
由於以下因素，以及影響我們財務狀況與營運成果的其他因素，我們過去的財務表現不應被視為未來表現的可靠指標，投資人亦不應以歷史趨勢預測未來期間的結果或趨勢。

在我們的三個營運分部中，收入與利潤來自基礎建設項目與服務，但我們並未直接控制這些基礎建設項目與服務的授予程序。建設產業歷來因經濟衰退、客戶業務週期低潮、供應鏈中斷與建築材料的價格或可得性、通貨膨脹壓力、利率波動、國際貿易問題（包括關稅與反關稅）、以及其他我們無法控制的經濟因素而經歷財務結果的週期性波動。許多因素，包括基礎建設產業的財務狀況，可能對我們的客戶及其未來資本支出的資金願景產生不利影響。此外，我們所服務產業中的併購、競爭或資本限制，可能會導致我們的客戶支出減少。
影響我們特定終端市場的經濟、法規與市場條件，可能對我們服務的需求產生不利影響，導致某些專案的延遲、減少或取消，且這些條件可能在未來繼續對我們產生不利影響。
執行我們專案所需的材料價格與可得性，受到我們無法控制的全球經濟因素影響，導致波動與中斷，包括但不限於人力短缺、工資壓力、通貨膨脹上升與潛在經濟放緩或衰退，以及燃料與能源成本、自然災害的影響、地緣政治衝突（例如東歐與中東的衝突），以及其他已影響或可能影響全球經濟的事件。如果材料短缺與成本上升以及勞動市場緊縮情況持續一段漫長時間，而我們無法彌補這些成本上升，我們的毛利率可能受到不利影響。
